doc.title: Mona Hinton interviewed by Milt Fillius and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Introduction and Mona honored at the Scottsdale Jazz Party
summary: Fillius introduces Mona; she explains she is the first woman and non-musician honored at the party. Brief mention of granddaughter Inez.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: We are about to do another videotape interview for the Jazz Archive of Hamilton College. We are very fortunate today to have with us Mona Hinton, who is the mother of all the jazz musicians in the U.S.A. She’s married to Milt, and very much acts the part and is the perfect musician’s wife. It’s a joy indeed to have her here representing all those great musicians’ wives. Mona, how are you today?

You’re doing fine, okay. And you’re being honored here at the Scottsdale Jazz Party at the Paradise Valley that is, and you are being honored, as was Milt some years ago, and I guarantee you it’s the only husband and wife team that will ever be honored in jazz, right?

Yes, well I have to — I must preface this — the reason I’m wearing my sweatshirt today that was specially designed for me. I think this is the eighteenth party that Don and Susan have given, and each year they’ve always honored a male musician. And I’m very happy to say that I am the first non-musician and the first female to be honored at this party so I think it’s quite an honor.

You have a lovely daughter, and a granddaughter whom I know you idolize, Inez. And I’m not going to ask you how she is because that would mean that we’d use the rest of the tape listening to stories about Inez. But I hope she is well.
